# Corriemount Abbey and Village: Side-Activity Menu (SEALED — DM ONLY)

> **Corriemount** (aka Corrie Mount, Cory Mount). A village and monastery of about 400 on Lake Corrie. Fog on the lake, bells, bees, honey-mead, a famous library.
> **Government:** **abbey rule.** The village and its lands belong to the **Abbey of the Still Lamp**, and the **Abbess, Mother Hilary Vance** (NPC-077), governs both. Gentle, unshakeable, genuinely good.
> **When visited:** optional, an Act II side thread (L7–13). **Tier: T2–T3.**
> **DM notes (world/03):** the founding monks were Wellgate-watchers; the order's original purpose was "keeping the lamp at the still water," forgotten into ritual. The library holds a Sundering-era account (seed). The cloister well is a minor Wellgate. **A faction inside the abbey has drifted toward the Calm** ("still water is holy"): the trusted-voucher pattern in miniature. Mother Hilary doesn't know.

---

## 1. The abbey at a glance

- **Look:** grey stone cloister on a green knoll above the lake; a squat bell tower with seven bells; beehives in neat white rows down the slope; the village below (thirty cottages, a mead-hall, a boathouse); on calm mornings the lake is so still it's a second sky.
- **Sound:** bells on the hours, bees all day, chanting at dusk.
- **Feel:** peaceful, slow, kind. The monks and sisters of the Still Lamp keep bees and books and a single oil lamp on the lakeshore that has (they say) never gone out.
- **The custom:** at dawn, the monks pray to the still lake. Visitors are welcome to sit with them. **Ash, sitting there, hears the faint hum of the cloister well** (no roll; the Wellgate). Don't explain it.

---

## 2. Shops and services

### 2.1 The Abbey Store (by the gatehouse)
**Keeper: Sister Winifred Oake** (NPC-335; aka Winnie, Winifred Oak), the bee-mistress and librarian, round-faced, sharp, laughs like a goose. The Still Lamp's best friend to visitors.
**Interior (painter):** a stone undercroft with honeycomb shelves (literally: real comb in glass), mead casks, wax candles by the hundred, bound books for sale on a lectern, a bee in amber on the counter.
**No haggling;** the abbey's prices are fixed and fair. Donations welcome.
| Item | Rarity | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Honey (a jar) · mead (a bottle) · beeswax candles (10) | mundane | 5 sp · 1 gp · 1 sp | The mead is famous. Gideon will buy a cask for Peg. |
| **Potion of Healing** (honey-based) | Common consumable | 50 gp | ×6; tastes wonderful |
| **Potion of Greater Healing** | Uncommon consumable | 200 gp | ×2 |
| **Candle of the Deep** | Common | 100 gp | Burns underwater |
| **Prayer bead** (a **Bead of Nourishment**) | Common consumable | 50 gp | |
| **Mead of Courage** (*Potion of Heroism*) | Uncommon consumable | 200 gp | ×1; Winifred makes one a year |
| Copies of abbey texts (scribed; a week) | mundane | 10–50 gp | Zeke |

### 2.2 The Library
Open to scholars by the Abbess's leave (**Persuasion DC 13**, or Zeke asking politely, no roll). Research here is at **advantage** for anything to do with the old orders, the Sundering, still water, or bees.
- **The Sundering-era account** (seed): a crumbling chronicle in the locked case. **Investigation DC 17** to find the right page; **Zeke** reads it (it's in an old script). It describes "the first watchers at the still water" who "kept the lamp lit so the waters would remember they were rivers." It names the order's founding charge: *keep the lamp at the still water*. (Fits SEC-02 and the Wellgate theme. Use only what the outline's secret seeds allow at that point.)

### 2.3 Healing (the infirmary)
Brother **Cuthbert** (no ID; Tier 3). *Cure Wounds* free for the poor, 10 gp otherwise; *Lesser Restoration* 40 gp; *Remove Curse* 90 gp; *Greater Restoration* 450 gp (T3).

## 3. Festivals and contests

### 3.1 Swarm Day (20 Seedtide)
The abbey's first bee-swarm of the year is "caught" by the whole village and walked to a new hive in procession, with bells. Afterward, a honey-feast on the green. **The Swarm Catch:** whoever coaxes the swarm into the skep wins the year's first honey and a seat at the Abbess's table. **Animal Handling DC 14**, then **Dexterity DC 13** (not to drop the skep), then **Constitution DC 12** (the stings). Moss automatically succeeds, and the bees settle on his coat like a cloak; the monks go very quiet.

### 3.2 The Bell-Ringers' Challenge (any feast day)
Ring the seven bells in the right changes. **The chain:** **Strength (Athletics) DC 13** (the big bell's rope) · **Wisdom (Perception) DC 14** (hear the pattern) · **Charisma (Performance) DC 15** (keep time) · **Constitution DC 13** (it takes an hour). **3–4:** the bells sing; the ringer's name goes on the tower board; **25 gp** from the village pot. **Ash's tune** rung on the seven bells makes the cloister well's water ripple (the monks see it; Ash hears it; the Calm faction notices *him*: a hook into §7).

### 3.3 The Library Riddle-Hunt (Harvest)
A riddle-trail through the library, set by Sister Winifred. Five riddles hidden in five books. **Intelligence (Investigation) DC 13 / 14 / 15 / 16 / 17**; Zeke has advantage on all. **Prize:** a **Spell Scroll** (3rd level: *Remove Curse* or *Sending*) and Winifred's lifelong friendship.

---


### Skill contests (`00-index.md` §11; CHG-21)
- **The Bell-Ringers' Challenge** (§3.2) runs as a **Mast Climb** (`00-index.md` §11.6) up the abbey tower: climb speed gives advantage on every stage.
- **Bee-Skep Archery** (archery, T2; feast days): straw skep-targets swung on ropes from the orchard trees (**moving, AC 15 / 16 / 17**), plus one long shot over the still lake (**AC 17 at 150 ft**, the monks' tradition). **Entry 5 gp; prize 60 gp and a jar of the abbey's honey.** Rival: Brother Gaskin, a lay brother who was a soldier (+7 ranged). *(The monks never let anyone shoot across the lake on calm mornings. They won't say why.)*

### New contests (`00-index.md` §13; CHG-22)
- **Candle-and-Bell: the Silent Crossing.** Cross the chapter house during vespers without ringing a bell or snuffing a candle; the abbot judges from the gallery. Prize: a blessing and a jar of the good honey (and the novices' undying respect).


## 4. Fights

**Ring formats (`00-index.md` §5.1, CHG-19):** there's no ring; brawls with pilgrims are **Last-Standing** rules if anyone's counting. No magic.

**None.** It's an abbey. A **Duel of Honor** isn't allowed on abbey land, so village disputes are settled by **the Long Silence**: both parties sit together in the chapel without speaking until one gives way. **Wisdom saves DC 12 / 14 / 16** each hour; the first to fail speaks first and loses. Ash will hate it. Gideon will win it.

---

## 5. Betting

Frowned on. The village does it anyway, in honey jars, at the mead-hall: on Swarm Day, the Bell-Ringers, and how long a visitor lasts in the Long Silence.

---

| 6 | (T3) The lakeshore lamp has gone out for the first time in four hundred years | the Abbess's trust | A seed-and-quest beat: someone *put it out*. §7. |

## 7. The Calm inside the abbey (the side thread)

**What's true:** **Prior Benedict Lowry** (NPC-334; aka Ben Lowery), the abbey's gentle, persuasive second-in-command, has been visiting Emberford's grief circles (FAC: the Calm) for two years. He believes, sincerely, that still water is holy, that the Calm's "stillness" is what the order's founders meant, and that the lakeshore lamp is a vanity. Six monks and sisters follow him. They practice "stilling" (the Calm's still-bowl meditation) in the cloister at night, at the well.
**The trusted-voucher pattern (in miniature):** **Mother Hilary vouches for Benedict** sincerely and warmly. She has a blind spot: he was her first novice, forty years ago, and she can't see him as anything but that boy. If Ash raises a concern, she defends him kindly and firmly. **No ledger edge exists for this pair yet** (`_change-requests.md` CHG-CY-03 proposes one; until it's added, play her public face: trusting, and never unkind).
**Seeds (place at least two before any reveal):** the novice in the fog (job 2); the bells rippling the well and a sister watching Ash too closely (§3.2); Benedict's hands, very still, always folded; Winifred's grumble that "the night office has got very quiet lately; nobody sings."
**Reveal options (any one):** catch the stilling at the well at night (**Stealth DC 15**, Bart, or Moss as an owl); Winifred's suspicion plus the library's founding charge (*keep the lamp lit*) set against Benedict's lamp being put out (job 6); or the novice, woken (**DC 17 Performance with the tune**), telling what she was taught.
**If the party digs early:** Benedict is gentle and open and has nothing to hide *that he knows is wrong*. He invites Ash to sit with them. **Wisdom save DC 15** or Ash feels very calm and very tired, and misses the next hour; nothing worse. He's not a villain. He's a good man who's wrong.
**Resolution:** Mother Hilary, shown the truth (EVT needed: log a new EVT when it happens), relights the lakeshore lamp herself, and asks Benedict to keep the night office *singing*. He weeps. Three of the six go back to the Calm in Emberford (a small Act II footprint). The abbey sends a cask of mead and three healer-monks to the Ch17 muster.
**Why this matters (fair in hindsight):** it's the campaign's big trusted-voucher twist in miniature. If the player plays it, they'll recognize the shape later and feel smart. If they skip it, nothing is lost.

---

## 8. Things worth stealing

Nothing. It's an abbey, and they'd give it to you if you asked. **Fence:** no.

---

## 9. Rivals

None, unless the player counts Brother Cuthbert, who has beaten every visitor at the Long Silence for twelve years.
